replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while preserving as much variance as possible. The basic steps involve standardizing the data, computing the covariance matrix, calculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, sorting the eigenvalues in descending order, and selecting the top k eigenvalues and their corresponding eigenvectors to form a feature vector. You then project the original data onto the new feature space. As for the mathematics, it can be quite complex, but you don't need to understand all the details to use PCA.
